- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.2) or flat — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; correct by reducing forecast peak after a spike (e.g., 2–3 days lag).
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show high prices, model often fails to revert — adjust downward by 1–2% per day.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model overestimates early in the window when sentiment is bullish, then underestimates later — apply “sentiment decay” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day after sentiment drops below 0.3.
- If sentiment is low and price is trending down, model often ignores the trend — add a downward bias of 0.5–1.0% per day to forecast.
